FOREWORD . ... .. .. ... ~-,..' :., .

This Indian Standard ( Third Revision) was adopted by Bureau of Indian Standards on 11 July 1989, after the draft finalized by Sewing Machine Sectional Committee, had been approved by Light Mechanical Engineering Division Council. This Standard was first published in 1959. It was subsequently revised in 1967 and 1974.

%'& third revision incorporates number of changes which were felt necessary as a result of frn-ther experience gained in the manufacture and use of presser feet and other development in the *M. The main modifications are:

a) Needle hole replaced by needle slot b) Stipulation c) Dimensional deleted. of specific material value of distance between contact face for thumb screw collar and presser bar

d) Reduced permissible variation between centre line of needle slot and contact face for presser bar. ln preparation of this standard, assistance has been derived from JIS B 9021-1960 `Presser foot of ming machine for home use' issued by Japanese Industrial Standard Committee.

HOUSEHOLD SEWING MACHINE - PRESSER FOOT - SPECIFICATION ( Third Revision )'
1 SCOPE 1.1This standard covers the requirements for presser foot for sewing machines for household purposes.
2 REFERENCES IS 1068 : 1985 Electroplated coatings of nickel plus chromium and copper plus nickel plus chromium on iron and steel ( second revision ) Method for vickers hardness for metallic materials : Part 1 HV 5 to HV 100 ( second revision ) Schedules for wrought steels for general engineering purposes : Part 2 Car( unalloyed steels bon steels) ( first revision ) Sampling inspection tables : Part 1 inspection by attributes and by count of defects ( first revision ) 4 MATERIAL

7 TOLERANCES 7.1 The side play between the presser foot top and bottom shall be such that presser foot bottom toe shall not deviate more than 0'4 mm in a horizontal plane.

8 WORKMANSHIP 8.1 The presser foot shall be finished to a smooth surface all over. 1

FIG. 1 NOMENCLATUREFOR PRESSER FOOT

IS : 1296 - 1989 8.2 The hinge action between presser foot top and presser foot bottom shall be smooth. 8.3 Sole side of the presser foot shall be smooth. 8.4 The contact face of the presser foot shall be smooth. 8.5 The presser foot shall be supplied in good quality chrome plated finish conforming to grade Fe/NQObCr of IS 1068 : 1968. 8.5.1 The plating shall be free from rust, blister, pits, cloudy patches, cracks, stains and other defects. 9 SAMPLING 9.1 Unless otherwise agreed between the supplier and the buyer the sampling Plan as given in For further inforAnnex A shall be followed. mations reference may be made to 1s 2500 ( Part 1) : 1973.
10 TEST 10.1 Presser

foot bottom shall not allow a tissue paper of 0'05 mm thickness to reach up to the needle point if it be inserted from any direction when the presser foot bottom is made to lie on the top surface of a reasonably flat needle plate.
11 MARKING 11.1 Presser foot may be marked manufacturer's name or trade mark. 12 PACKING

with

the

12.1Presser foot coated with antirust oil shall be securely,packed in strong cardboard cartons in accordance with the best prevalent trade practice. Each carton shall bear the manufacturer's name or trade-mark, type and the description of contents.
